title: An operator-written gloss is labeled cited_passage
description:
Cycle-25 High, reproduced. NOT a tampered-index defect: it is reachable through
the documented spec format in ordinary use, which makes it more serious than the
whole tampered-index sequence cycles 17-24 closed.

A note-backed constraint or prior decision may carry an optional operator
`statement`. The builder copies that operator-authored gloss into `statement`
and then labels the WHOLE item evidence_class "cited_passage". Nothing checks
that the cited passage says anything like the gloss.

Reproduced with an ordinary spec, no tampering:

  vault section : "We evaluated three vendors and picked none of them yet."
  operator gloss: "This architecture decision was approved."
  emitted       : evidence_class='cited_passage', citation='Notes.md:8-8',
                  statement='This architecture decision was approved.'

Worse than the reviewer described: the Markdown projection does NOT project
`passage` for constraints and prior decisions, so a reader of the artifact sees
only the operator's sentence, a real citation, and the label "cited_passage".
The passage that contradicts it is never shown. The rendered block reads:

  Constraint 1 statement:  ```text This architecture decision was approved. ```
  Constraint 1 citation:   ```text Notes.md:8-8 ```
  Constraint 1 evidence class: ```text cited_passage ```

This blurs authored assertion and cited evidence, which is the project's central
evidence boundary, and it contradicts ARCHITECTURE.md's claim that RecallWeave
never infers that a passage is a constraint or a decision. Here it does worse
than infer: it attributes the operator's words to the vault.

The existing suite PINS the behaviour rather than rejecting it
(tests/test_contract_document.py: passage equals the indexed section while the
statement is separately expected to be the operator gloss).
design:
Needs a decision on the evidence model before implementation. Three options:

A. RECOMMENDED. Classify by who wrote the statement, not by whether a citation
   is attached. A note-backed item WITH an operator statement is
   authored_by_operator, and its citation/passage travel as SUPPORTING evidence
   in their own fields, visibly separate from the assertion. Only an item whose
   statement IS the cited passage keeps cited_passage. This preserves both
   pieces of information and puts the label on the right thing.
B. Reject the combination: a note-backed selector may not also carry an operator
   statement. Simplest and fully honest, but it removes a documented spec
   capability operators may rely on.
C. Project `passage` for constraints and prior decisions so a reader at least
   sees the gloss and the passage side by side. Weaker: the evidence_class label
   is still wrong, and injectivity/partition tests would need updating.

Whichever is chosen, add the reviewer's tests: a note-backed constraint whose
passage does not assert the gloss must not be classified cited_passage; the same
for prior decisions; and a test that every cited_passage statement is itself
copied from the cited passage rather than merely accompanied by one.

Note the projected-field consequences: constraints[].passage and
prior_decisions[].passage are currently DOCUMENTED AS OMITTED from the Markdown
(see the omitted list in docs/task-contracts.md). Option A or C changes that
partition, so the partition test and the omitted list must move together.
acceptance_criteria: A note-backed constraint whose passage does not assert the operator gloss is NOT classified cited_passage; same for a prior decision. Every cited_passage statement is itself copied from the cited passage rather than merely accompanied by one. The existing test that pins the current behaviour is updated rather than left contradicting the new rule. Docs and ARCHITECTURE.md agree with the code. Full suite green.
notes: OWNS: src/recallweave/contract.py, tests/test_contract_document.py, tests/test_contract_projection.py, docs/task-contracts.md, ARCHITECTURE.md
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Evidence class now names the origin of the statement: operator wording stays authored_by_operator even when cited, cited_passage means the statement IS the passage, and the Markdown projects the supporting passage under its own label. truncated/passage_truncated split. No semantic-support inference added. Four mutations killed. Suite 417 green.

title: Heading-link re-derivation cannot bind the coordinate or heading level
description:
Cycle-24 High, reproduced. The eighth "one level below", introduced by the
recallweave-5sy heading route.

_matching_links_in_heading binds the heading TEXT to sections.heading and parses
the supplied source_text for the link, but never uses persisted["line"]. The
sections table records a body's line_start and line_end and NEVER the heading's
own physical line or its '#' level.

Reproduced against a real index whose only link is on the heading '## A
[[Target]]':

  claimed line 1       -> ACCEPTED
  claimed line 999999  -> ACCEPTED
  '###### A [[Target]]' instead of '## A [[Target]]' -> ACCEPTED
  claimed line 8 (a real body line)                  -> rejected

So a tampered index can pair an authentic indexed heading with a false
coordinate, or change the heading level, and the export accepts it. The heading
text, link kind, link target and unique resolution ARE bound, so a heading link
cannot be invented -- only mis-coordinated.

The documentation over-claim was fixed immediately (docs/task-contracts.md and
CHANGELOG.md now disclose the gap, pinned by a docs test). This bead tracks the
remaining binding.
design:
DEFERRED BY JOSH 2026-08-22 as follow-up, not blocking this session's work.
Promotion to main stays blocked until it lands.

The exporter cannot close this from the index as it stands: sections has no
column for a heading's physical line or its level. The three options weighed
were:

1. Bind what is derivable (the claimed line must fall in the window between the
   previous section's line_end and this section's line_start, and source_text
   must equal '#'*n + ' ' + the stored heading for some n in 1..6). Narrows the
   gap without closing it -- the exact line within the window and the level stay
   unbound.
2. Reject heading-line authored edges outright. Fully honest, but refuses the
   whole export for a legitimate vault whose link sits on a heading, which is
   the false rejection recallweave-5sy fixed, reinstated deliberately.
3. RECORD the heading's physical line and level in the sections table. Closes it
   properly and permanently, and makes a heading link bind exactly like a body
   link. Cost: a core index schema change and a re-index for existing users.

Option 3 is the real fix and the reason this is deferred rather than patched:
it belongs with a core index schema revision, not inside the task-contract
work, and the current session froze schema_version "2".

Whoever picks this up: decide the schema change first, then make
_matching_links_in_heading bind the coordinate and the level exactly, and delete
the disclosure paragraph in docs/task-contracts.md ("only partly bound, and this
is a known gap") along with its docs test.
acceptance_criteria: A genuine heading link whose persisted line is changed to 1, to 999999, or to another real body line is rejected. A heading link whose marker count is altered is rejected. Two identical headings at different coordinates cannot authenticate each other. A mutation removing the coordinate predicate fails the new test. The disclosure paragraph and its docs test are removed once the property holds. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. sections now records heading_line and heading_level; the exporter reconstructs the heading line from indexed data and requires the quoted text to equal it at the claimed coordinate. Public SCHEMA_VERSION deliberately unchanged; a capability PRAGMA refuses an index that predates the columns. Four mutations killed; disclosure paragraph removed and its docs test inverted. Suite 420 green.

title: Authored-link re-derivation loses the indexer's parser state
description:
Cycle-23 High. The seventh "one level below", and this time it also exposed a
FALSE REJECTION I had introduced.

_authored_link_is_rederivable called parser._links on ONE ISOLATED LINE, but
_links tracks fenced-code state ACROSS lines. Link-looking text inside an open
fence is ignored by the indexer and was accepted by the exporter as proof of an
authored, verified relationship.

Reproduced: a source note whose only wikilink sits inside a ``` fence produces
ZERO authored edges from the indexer, yet a hand-inserted edge citing that line
exported as verified.

Found here while building the fix: parsing only section BODIES also rejected a
GENUINE edge. The indexer finds links on HEADING lines too, and a heading line
is not in any section's text -- the index keeps it in sections.heading. A vault
whose only link is on a heading line therefore failed to export at all. That is
the opposite failure and just as bad.

A section can also hold BOTH a fenced link and a real one, so re-derivation must
bind to the link at the CLAIMED line rather than to any matching link elsewhere
in the same section.
design:
Parse INDEXED text with the parser's own state, by both routes the indexer uses.

1. Section body: parse the WHOLE covering section with _links, not one line, so
   fenced-code state is what the indexer saw. Require the quoted source text to
   be the exact physical line at the claimed coordinate, and require the
   extracted link to be AT that line with matching kind and target.
2. Heading: when no section covers the claimed line, bind the quoted source text
   to a stored sections.heading (its leading '#' markers removed) before parsing
   it. The text then comes from the index rather than from the edge, and a
   heading inside a fence never becomes a section, so a stored heading is by
   construction outside fenced code.
3. Keep resolution through index._resolve_link with uniqueness, unchanged.
4. Document the parser-state property and pin it with a docs test, because the
   reason the whole section is parsed is not obvious from the code alone.
acceptance_criteria: Tests reject a wikilink, a markdown link, a tilde-fenced link and a heading-looking line inside a fence, each verified first to produce ZERO authored edges from the real indexer; reject a claim quoting a fenced line in a section that also holds a real link; and reject a heading the index does not hold. A genuine heading-line link still exports. Mutations restoring isolated-line parsing, unbinding the claimed line within the section, unbinding the heading from the index, or removing the heading route each fail. Docs describe the parser-state rule, pinned by a docs test. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Whole-section parsing restores the indexer's fenced-code state; heading-line links re-derive via sections.heading, fixing a false rejection found while building the fix. Four mutations killed; every fence test first proves the indexer creates no edge. Suite 411 green.

title: Authored-link re-derivation checks the parts, not the binding
description:
Cycle-22 High and Medium.

The recallweave-o6r "re-derivation" was not one. _authored_link_is_rederivable
checked the parts INDEPENDENTLY -- that source_text was some substring of the
covering section, and that target_text resolved to the target note -- and never
established that the source line contained a link at all, that the link pointed
at that target, or that its syntax matched the declared kind.

The reviewer's reproduction: a source section line reading "This line contains
no link at all." with target_text "Target" authenticated as an authored,
verified relationship between unlinked notes.

Two further weaknesses in the same routine:
- name resolution accepted any matching note_names row without requiring the
  normalized name to resolve UNIQUELY, while the indexer rejects ambiguity;
- path resolution used suffix matching, broader than _resolve_link's exact
  vault-relative and source-relative keys.

Medium: the docs called a candidate's persisted score "a cosine score" while
the exporter only checks it is finite and in (0, 1], and the CHANGELOG claimed
a hand-written verified relationship could no longer export, which was false.
design:
Re-derive the BINDING, using the indexer's own code rather than a parallel
matcher that can drift from it.

1. Read the EXACT physical line back out of the indexed section that covers the
   claimed coordinate (sections.text holds lines line_start..line_end in order)
   and require the quoted source_text to be that line, not any nearby text.
2. Parse that one line with parser._links -- the indexer's own extractor -- and
   require an extracted link whose kind equals the edge's kind and whose target
   equals target_text.
3. Resolve that link with index._resolve_link -- the indexer's own resolver --
   and require exactly one candidate, no ambiguity reason, and that the
   candidate is this edge's target note. De-duplicate the note_names lookup per
   normalized name: one note contributes several rows (title and stem), and
   without de-duplication a single unambiguous note looks like two candidates
   and every genuine link is rejected.
4. Everything reads the INDEX. _links runs over one line already stored in
   sections.text, so the exporter still performs no file reads.
5. Correct the docs and CHANGELOG: describe a candidate's score as persisted
   and range-checked rather than as a recomputed cosine, and say so where the
   connections contract is first described, not only in a later section.
acceptance_criteria: Tests reject a line containing no link, a link whose target disagrees with the edge endpoint, wikilink syntax declared as a markdown link, a target name appearing as prose, a quoted source text belonging to another line of the same section, and an ambiguous target name tried against BOTH ambiguous endpoints. Each FAILS against the current tree. A genuine authored link still exports. Mutations removing the link/kind/target binding, the uniqueness rule, or the exact-physical-line rule each fail. Docs and CHANGELOG describe the score as persisted and range-checked, pinned by a docs test. Full suite green.
notes: OWNS: src/recallweave/contract.py, tests/test_contract_document.py, tests/test_docs_per_field_projection.py, docs/task-contracts.md, CHANGELOG.md
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Authored links now re-derive through the indexer's own extractor and resolver against the exact physical indexed line, with uniqueness enforced. Five mutations killed. Score wording corrected in docs and CHANGELOG and pinned by tests. Suite 408 green.

title: Persisted edge identity and classification are unauthenticated
description:
Cycle-21 High and Medium, all four scenarios reproduced locally (the reviewer
could not, being sandboxed read-only).

  1. arbitrary score 99.5                 -> EXPORTED score=99.5
  2. kind='human_verified'                -> EXPORTED kind='human_verified',
                                             class still 'discovery_candidate'
  3. hand-inserted is_verified=1 row with
     empty evidence between two unlinked
     notes                                -> EXPORTED as class='authored_link',
                                             verified=True
  4. all candidates rewritten as verified
     with empty evidence                  -> EXPORTED, all class='authored_link'

The fifth "one level below". Cycles 17-20 authenticated the evidence PAYLOAD --
citations, passages, headings, truncation, shared terms, method, explanation.
The record that BINDS a payload to a pair of notes and declares its class was
still copied straight out of the edges row. The schema constrains only
is_verified to 0/1: not kind, not score, not their consistency.

Scenarios 3 and 4 are the severe ones. They let a row that nothing supports be
presented as an authored, verified relationship, which is precisely the
verified-versus-candidate boundary this project exists to keep visible.

Medium: the documentation described emitted connections as authored verified
edges or lexical candidates and presented vocabulary and constants as sufficient
authentication, without disclosing that the classifications themselves were
unauthenticated.
design:
APPROVED BY JOSH 2026-08-22: envelope rules plus authored-link re-derivation.
NOT full recomputation.

1. Declare the envelope as data, like CONNECTION_EVIDENCE_APPLICABILITY:
   AUTHORED_LINK_KINDS = {wikilink, markdown_link}, CANDIDATE_KIND =
   "discovery_candidate", AUTHORED_EVIDENCE_MEMBERS = {line:int,
   source_text:str, target_text:str}.
2. A candidate must carry kind=CANDIDATE_KIND, is_verified=0, and a finite
   cosine score in (0, 1].
3. An authored edge must carry a kind in AUTHORED_LINK_KINDS, is_verified=1,
   score exactly 1.0, and must RE-DERIVE from the index: persisted evidence has
   exactly the three members with correct types; the source note has an indexed
   section covering `line` whose text contains `source_text`; and `target_text`
   resolves to the target note by normalized name or by path, the same two
   routes _resolve_link takes.
4. Validate the envelope BEFORE the payload, so class is established before
   anything is judged by class. Fail closed with the established content-free
   diagnostic.
5. Do NOT recompute candidate existence, the score threshold or the bounded
   top-per-note selection. That duplicates index.py in the exporter and makes
   export time scale with index size. Document the boundary explicitly instead:
   a candidate is checked to be shaped and evidenced like one the indexer
   produces, not to be one the indexer did produce.
acceptance_criteria: Tests reject an arbitrary, negative and zero candidate score, a fabricated candidate kind, a candidate promoted to verified, a rewritten authored score and kind, and six forged authored-link shapes including empty evidence; each FAILS against the current tree and the diagnostic names only the edge id. A test proves a genuine index still exports BOTH evidence classes. Mutations removing the envelope gate, the authored re-derivation, the candidate kind/score rules or the source-text containment check each fail. Docs state precisely what is and is not authenticated. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Edge envelope declared as data and validated before the payload; authored links re-derive from the indexed section text and note-name resolution. Candidate existence/ranking deliberately not recomputed and documented as such. Four mutations killed; a genuine index still exports both classes. Suite 404 green.

title: Discovery-candidate evidence accepts empty or fabricated shared_terms
description:
Cycle-20 High plus its Medium, reproduced. The FOURTH "one level below": the
citation work authenticated the passages, while the sibling members that make
an edge a discovery_candidate stayed only superficially typed.

Reproduced on the current tree:

  persisted []                          -> emitted []                    well_formed=True
  persisted [1, {"vault": "secret"}]    -> emitted []                    well_formed=True
  persisted ["fabricated-term","another-fake"] -> emitted unchanged      well_formed=True
  persisted ["zephyr"]                  -> emitted ["zephyr"]            well_formed=True

and a full export with shared_terms ["fabricated-term","another-fake"],
method "forged" and explanation "forged" SUCCEEDED.

So a persisted edge could claim any vocabulary at all -- including terms chosen
to make an unrelated pair look related -- or none, and still export as a valid
discovery_candidate rendering exactly like a real one. The citation checks
authenticate the passages but not the asserted RELATIONSHIP between them.

index.py refuses to create a candidate from fewer than two shared terms, and
ARCHITECTURE.md promises "at least two informative shared terms". _edge_evidence
also silently filters non-string elements, so corruption arrives as a well-typed
empty list rather than as an error.

Medium, same root: the suite BLESSED the contradiction. One test declared that
emitted shared_terms can never be empty and carries the terms the candidate was
found by; another explicitly expected {"shared_terms": []} to be well formed.
design:
Authenticate the candidate envelope the way the sides are authenticated.

1. Predicate level (no index needed): shared_terms must be a list of at least
   MIN_SHARED_TERMS (2) non-empty strings. method and explanation are REQUIRED
   for discovery_candidate and must equal the indexer's own values, declared as
   INDEX_CANDIDATE_METHOD and INDEX_CANDIDATE_EXPLANATION.
2. Index level: every claimed term must be one BOTH endpoint notes carry in the
   terms table. Do NOT recompute the TF-IDF ranking inside the exporter; check
   the weaker sufficient property that the ranking is a selection from the
   shared vocabulary.
3. Check the PERSISTED shared_terms list for non-string elements directly, since
   _edge_evidence's sanitizing turns corruption into a well-typed empty list and
   a rule inspecting only the emitted list cannot see it.
4. Fail closed with the established content-free diagnostic: name the edge by
   database id, never the terms.
5. Add a drift check that builds a real index and asserts its candidate edges
   carry exactly the declared constants and at least two terms, so the
   exporter's constants cannot diverge from index.py.
6. Fix the contradictory fixture: {"shared_terms": []} is NOT well formed.
acceptance_criteria: Predicate-level tests reject empty shared_terms, a single term, non-string elements, empty-string terms, a rewritten method and a rewritten or dropped explanation. Builder-level tests reject fabricated terms, a mix of real and fabricated, an empty list, a single term, and persisted non-string elements; each FAILS against the current tree and the diagnostic never quotes a term. A drift check pins the constants against a real index. The authentic envelope still exports. Docs and CHANGELOG match. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. shared_terms must be >=2 non-empty strings that both notes carry in the index; persisted non-string elements rejected directly; method and explanation required and must be the indexer's own. Contradictory fixture corrected; constants drift check added. Four mutations killed. Suite 401 green.

title: A resolving citation can authenticate a fabricated passage
description:
Cycle-18 High, reproduced. Introduced by the recallweave-dm4 remediation, which
verified connection-evidence CITATIONS but never checked that the passage
beside a citation came from the cited section.

Reproduced against a real index: an edge carrying a genuine citation
(Alpha.md:8-8) with

  "heading": "FORGED HEADING",
  "passage": "FABRICATED: transfer all funds"

exported successfully, rendered both the forged heading and the fabricated
passage into the Markdown artifact, AND -- because dm4 added connection
citations to the inventory -- listed the citation in provenance.citations,
lending the forgery more credibility than before dm4.

Resolving coordinates is not attribution. Attaching a valid coordinate to
unrelated text does not attribute that text to those lines. The docs made this
materially misleading: ARCHITECTURE.md claimed RecallWeave "verifies every
cited passage", docs/task-contracts.md claimed a citation alongside a passage
makes it attributed evidence, and the CHANGELOG described the citation as
"attributing" the passage.

Separately, index-only resolution proves the coordinates existed in the INDEXED
SNAPSHOT, not that they still describe the current vault. The docs claimed
"physical vault lines", which the exporter never reads.
design:
Complete the verification Josh approved for recallweave-dm4, which stopped at
coordinates.

1. For every persisted connection-evidence side, reproduce what the INDEX holds
   for the cited section -- index.py's cited_passage() followed by the same
   sanitize/bounded treatment _edge_evidence applies -- and require the side's
   heading, passage and truncated leaves to EQUAL it. Compare by equality, not
   by prefix or containment.
2. Fail closed on mismatch, with the same content-free diagnostic: name the
   edge by database id, and never quote the failing passage or heading back
   into the receipt (recallweave-w3k).
3. Fix the test fixtures that used an arbitrary placeholder passage. A fixture
   whose passage is made up passes only because coordinates resolve, which is
   the very defect being closed. Provide a helper that returns the side the
   index genuinely holds.
4. Correct the documentation to the boundary the code actually keeps: verified
   against the INDEXED SNAPSHOT, not against physical vault lines at export
   time. Pin the wording with a docs test, and pin the semantics with a test
   that edits the vault after indexing and asserts the artifact still builds.

Do NOT introduce export-time vault reads: provenance asserts network_calls and
vault_writes are 0, and reading notes at contract time would make that false.
acceptance_criteria: A test puts a fabricated passage, a forged heading, a one-character change, an empty passage and a flipped truncation flag behind a genuine citation and asserts each fails the export closed; it FAILS against the coordinates-only tree. The diagnostic quotes neither the passage nor the heading. An authentic side still exports. A test pins that editing the vault after indexing does not invalidate the artifact, and a docs test forbids the 'physical vault lines' wording. Full suite green.
notes: OWNS: src/recallweave/contract.py, tests/test_contract_document.py, tests/test_docs_per_field_projection.py, docs/task-contracts.md, ARCHITECTURE.md
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Connection-evidence sides are now attributed by content (heading, passage, truncated compared by equality against what the index holds), not just by coordinates. Diagnostic stays content-free. Placeholder fixtures replaced. Docs corrected from 'physical vault lines' to the indexed-snapshot boundary and pinned by a docs test. Three mutations killed. Suite 393 green.

title: Connection-evidence citations are neither verified nor inventoried
description:
Cycle-17 High, reproduced. Predates this session; sixteen review cycles missed
it.

ARCHITECTURE.md says RecallWeave "verifies every cited passage resolves to
physical vault lines" and docs/task-contracts.md says provenance.citations
"lists every citation in document order, deduplicated". Connection-evidence
citations honour neither claim:

- _edge_evidence accepts ANY string as source_evidence.citation /
  target_evidence.citation; connection_evidence_is_well_formed checks only that
  it is a str.
- provenance.citations is built solely from constraints, prior decisions and
  retrieved context, so connection-evidence citations never appear in it.

Reproduced: a persisted discovery edge carrying

  {"shared_terms": ["zephyr"],
   "source_evidence": {"citation": "Nonexistent.md:999-1000",
                       "passage": "purported evidence"}}

is accepted, emitted, and RENDERED into the Markdown artifact, while
provenance.citations omits it. A receiving agent sees purported cited evidence
that RecallWeave neither resolved nor recorded, rendered identically to a
verified citation.

Related, same reproduction run: a side carrying a `passage` with NO `citation`
also passes well-formedness, despite the "cited passage" framing throughout the
docs. That is unattributed quoted evidence.
design:
APPROVED BY JOSH 2026-08-22: VERIFY AND INVENTORY. Also: require a citation
alongside any passage.

1. Resolve every connection-evidence citation against the INDEX, not the vault
   (the exporter must keep network_calls and vault_writes at 0). A citation
   resolves iff it parses as `<relative_path>:<start>-<end>` and some section
   satisfies notes.relative_path = path AND sections.line_start = start AND
   sections.line_end = end. That is exactly the form the builder itself mints
   (contract.py builds `f"{relative_path}:{line_start}-{line_end}"` from a
   chosen section), and it was verified against the real fixtures: every
   persisted evidence citation in both test indexes matches a section exactly,
   so this rejects no healthy index.

2. FAIL CLOSED on a citation that does not resolve, consistent with
   recallweave-4su, and keep the diagnostic CONTENT-FREE per recallweave-w3k:
   name the edge by its database id, never the citation or the path.

3. Add the connection-evidence citations of ADMITTED connections to
   provenance.citations, in document order (source side then target side, after
   retrieved context, which is the order the sections render in), deduplicated
   against what is already there.

4. Strengthen well-formedness: a side carrying `passage` must also carry
   `citation`. This tightens the rule in the SAME direction as the existing
   substantive-leaf requirement, so it does not reopen recallweave-6j3.

Do not change budget semantics here. Citations are uncharged uniformly today
(retrieved-context citations already reach provenance.citations without their
own charge); making them charged is a separate decision.
acceptance_criteria: A test persists a discovery edge whose connection-evidence citation is syntactically valid but resolves to nothing, calls the public builder, and asserts it raises; the test FAILS against the current tree. A second test asserts provenance.citations contains every connection-evidence citation of every admitted connection, in document order, deduplicated across constraints, prior decisions, retrieved context and connections. A third asserts a side with a passage and no citation is rejected. The diagnostic still names the edge by id and carries no path or citation text. A healthy index still exports unchanged. Docs match the code. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Connection-evidence citations are resolved against the index (exact section match, index-only), fail closed when unresolvable with a content-free diagnostic, and are inventoried in provenance.citations in document order. Passage now requires a citation. Five mutations killed. Cycle-17 Medium (CHANGELOG over-claim on whole-index validation) also fixed and pinned by a docs test. Suite 390 green.

title: Malformed-evidence diagnostic discloses vault note paths
description:
Cycle-15 High, reproduced. Introduced by the recallweave-4su remediation
itself.

build_contract_document() raises ValueError naming the offending connection by
its vault-relative endpoint PATHS, and cli.py serializes the message verbatim
into the structured stderr receipt. Vault-relative paths are vault-derived
metadata: they can disclose people, health information, legal matters, projects
and organizational structure. PRIVACY.md already recognizes relative paths as
sensitive bundle content but says nothing about failure receipts carrying them.

Reproduced: a vault holding People/Medical Diagnosis.md and Legal/Acquisition
Target.md, with a malformed persisted edge between them, produces

  malformed connection evidence in the index for
  Legal/Acquisition Target.md -> People/Medical Diagnosis.md
  (discovery_candidate): ...

on stderr, with exit code 2 and no artifact written. The disclosure happens on
the failure path, where no bundle is produced at all and the operator has
consented to nothing.

The CLI test added with the fix asserts the error route works but never asserts
that endpoint names are absent from it.
design:
Identify the offending edge by a NON-CONTENT-BEARING identifier: the edges
table's primary key, available as row["id"] because _edge_rows selects e.*.
The message keeps the evidence_class (a fixed enum, not vault-derived) and the
remediation advice, and drops both paths.

An operator can resolve the id against their own local index if they want the
endpoints; the diagnostic itself no longer carries vault content into a
receipt, a log, or a terminal transcript that may be shared.

Excluded endpoints already cannot reach this diagnostic -- an excluded edge is
`continue`d before validation -- but pin that with a test rather than leaving
it to inference.

title: Absence marker is in-band: a value equal to 'None recorded.' is indistinguishable from absence
description:
Found by coordinator mutation audit (not previously reported by Codex). A TRUE injectivity violation over WELL-FORMED documents, with no qualification available -- not 'up to line-ending normalization', not a malformed-shape excuse.

Reproduced on foundry/task-contracts:

  NONE_RECORDED = 'None recorded.'
  handling.scope = None                vs  handling.scope = 'None recorded.'
    -> byte-identical render: True
  exclusions.paths = None              vs  exclusions.paths = ['None recorded.']
    -> byte-identical render: True

Cause: _field() renders absence by placing the trusted marker string INSIDE the fence as ordinary content:
    content = _as_str(value) if value is not None else NONE_RECORDED
    return [_literal(label), _fenced_esc(content)]
The marker therefore lives in the SAME value space as untrusted content. Any real value that happens to equal the marker imitates absence perfectly. This is classic in-band signalling, and it is the same class of defect the uniform-inert-rendering design was adopted to eliminate: the whole point of that design is that trusted chrome and untrusted values never share a channel. Absence is currently signalled in the untrusted channel.

REACHABLE through the public API: the objective and acceptance statements are operator-authored free text, and passages are vault text. A note or spec containing the literal words 'None recorded.' produces the collision. No hostile intent required.

The mutation audit shows the surrounding invariants ARE otherwise well enforced -- 11 of 15 mutations were caught, including absence-vs-empty-string, merged fences, dropped fields and doc/test drift -- so this is a specific hole, not general weakness.
design: Make absence STRUCTURAL rather than a magic string, so no value can imitate it. The natural form given the existing design: a present field always renders its label followed by a fenced block; an absent field renders its label followed by a trusted marker line OUTSIDE any fence (or no fenced block at all). Because every present value always produces a fence, and the absence marker never does, no content can forge absence. That keeps the inertness invariant intact -- the marker is renderer-authored chrome, and values stay fenced -- while moving the signal out of the untrusted channel. Do NOT fix this by escaping or by picking a more exotic marker string; any in-band sentinel is forgeable and this class of fix has already failed repeatedly in this project.
acceptance_criteria: A field whose value is exactly 'None recorded.' renders DIFFERENTLY from that field being absent, for every projected scalar field and for collection elements. A test pins both the scalar and the collection case and FAILS against the current tree before the fix. Absence remains distinguishable from an empty string. Parser-backed inertness still holds: the absence marker is chrome, every document-derived value is still fenced. Full suite green with the parser.

Three mutation-proven tests (all-fields inequality, all-fields structural, parser-backed channel check) fail against the pre-fix tree and also kill an exotic-in-band-sentinel fix. title: Well-formedness must reach inside evidence sides, not just top-level members
description:
Cycle-13 Codex High, reproduced by the coordinator with the exact shape Codex reported:

  a = evidence {shared_terms:[x]}
  b = evidence {shared_terms:[x], source_evidence:{truncated:true}}
  a well_formed = True
  b well_formed = True
  byte_identical = True

Two documents that differ in a real field are BOTH classified well-formed and render byte for byte the same, so the injectivity claim is still false.

Cause: connection_evidence_is_well_formed() validates only the presence/absence of the three TOP-LEVEL evidence members. It never validates the CONTENTS of a side. contract_markdown.py:218 renders only citation/heading/passage from a side, so a side carrying nothing else -- for example only 'truncated' -- renders as nothing and is indistinguishable from an absent side.

This is builder-reachable, not a hand-crafted-dict problem: _edge_evidence (contract.py:96) independently retains any subset of citation, heading and passage, plus truncated. A partial side is a document a caller can actually obtain.

Related Medium, same root cause: the applicability table governs only the three top-level members, _EVIDENCE_MEMBERS at contract.py:38 is UNUSED, and nested side applicability and types stay implicit in _edge_evidence and the renderer. Validity is therefore not decidable from the table alone, contrary to the claim.

This is the THIRD consecutive cycle where the same pattern recurs: an invariant asserted at one level while the defect lives one level below it. Fix the depth, not just this instance.
design:
Two parts.

(1) DEPTH. Extend the applicability table to cover side-level leaves, not just top-level members, and make it the single source of truth actually consumed by both the builder-side validator and the tests. Delete or use _EVIDENCE_MEMBERS; an unused constant advertising itself as the source of truth is worse than none. Well-formedness must then be decidable from the table alone for the whole nested shape.

(2) THE UNPROJECTED SIDE MEMBER. Side-level 'truncated' is in the document, is builder-reachable, and influences nothing in the projection -- that is exactly the injectivity hole. RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION, following the precedent Josh set for recallweave-ah5 (render and document rather than hide): PROJECT side-level truncated. A reader who is shown a passage should be told it was cut; hiding that is an evidence-integrity loss in a project whose premise is evidence integrity. Additionally require that a PRESENT side carries at least one projected leaf, so an empty-in-effect side cannot masquerade as an absent one. If instead it is decided not to project it, then it must be documented as not-projected AND a side carrying only unprojected members must be rejected as malformed -- silence is not an option.
acceptance_criteria: The reproduction above no longer holds: the two documents are distinguishable -- either b is rejected as malformed or it renders differently -- and a test pins that exact pair, failing against the current tree first. The applicability table covers nested side leaves and is consumed by the validator rather than duplicated in prose. _EVIDENCE_MEMBERS is used or removed. Negative cases prove rejection for: a partial side, a side containing only truncated, a non-dict side, shared_terms that is None or a non-list, and an unknown evidence member. description: Operator decision after six adversarial review cycles each found another context-specific escaping defect. Context-specific escaping is abandoned. design:
# FROZEN INTERFACE v3 — uniform inert Markdown rendering

Supersedes v2 section A and v1 section 8. Everything else in v1/v2 stands.
Six consecutive adversarial reviews each found one more context-specific escaping
defect: block structure, inline constructs, handling routing, the multiline citation
branch, bare CR, and indented markers inside a blockquote. Context-specific escaping is
now abandoned by operator decision.

## A. The invariant

**No operator-controlled or vault-derived string may ever be interpreted as Markdown
syntax.**

This is absolute. Human readability may not weaken it. The structured JSON document
`recallweave.contract.v1` is the canonical contract; the Markdown artifact is a SAFE
HUMAN-READABLE PROJECTION of it. A richer human presentation, if ever wanted, is a
separate renderer built from the structured contract — never a relaxation of this one.

## B. The mechanism

Exactly two categories of text exist in the rendered document.

1. **Trusted chrome** — string literals authored in `contract_markdown.py` itself:
   the eight section headings, field labels, table-free item labels, and the
   `None recorded.` placeholder. These are live Markdown. They never interpolate a
   value from the document.
2. **Untrusted values** — every string that arrives from the document, without
   exception: objective, task id, acceptance statements, constraint and decision
   statements, citations, passages, connection endpoints/kinds/scores, exclusion
   paths/globs/tags/directives, provenance values, budget numbers, disclosure values,
   and both handling strings. Every one of these is emitted ONLY inside a fenced code
   block.

Fence rule (unchanged and now the whole safety story): the opening fence is a run of
backticks strictly longer than the longest backtick run anywhere in the content, with a
minimum of three, and the info string is the literal `text`. Content is emitted verbatim
after normalizing CRLF and bare CR to LF. Because the opening fence is longer than any
run inside, no content line can close it, and nothing inside a fenced block is parsed as
Markdown.

Nothing untrusted appears outside a fence. Not in a heading, not in a table cell, not in
a list item, not in a blockquote, not in a link, not in an info string.

## C. Consequences that are approved appearance changes

These follow from the invariant and are deliberate. Update the docs to match; do not
preserve prettier output at the cost of the invariant.

- The document title becomes the trusted literal `# Task contract`. The task id and
  objective move into fenced blocks under section 1.
- Acceptance criteria stop being a `- [ ]` checklist of interpolated text. Each becomes
  a trusted label line followed by a fenced block.
- Constraints and prior decisions stop putting citations in inline code spans. Each item
  becomes a trusted label line followed by one fenced block carrying the statement and,
  on its own line, the citation.
- The connections **table is removed**. A table cannot contain a fenced block, so a table
  cannot hold untrusted values safely. Each connection becomes a trusted label followed by
  a fenced block.
- Retrieved-context `### <citation>` headings become trusted `### Passage N` headings,
  with the citation inside the fenced block.
- The handling blockquote is removed; both handling strings are fenced.

The eight numbered sections and their order do not change.

## D. The authoritative test: parse the AST

String heuristics are no longer the gate; they proved to share the renderer's blind
spots twice (the LF-only oracle missed bare CR, the line-prefix oracle missed indented
markers inside a blockquote). Keep useful direct-string regression tests, but structural
parser validation is authoritative.

Selected parser: **mistletoe** (pure Python, CommonMark-compliant, ZERO required runtime
dependencies, actively maintained, exposes a walkable token tree). Verified to detect the
current defect: it reports `Heading` and `List` tokens nested inside `Quote` for the
cycle-6 payload.

Declare it as a TEST-ONLY optional dependency; runtime install stays dependency-free:

    [project.optional-dependencies]
    test = ["mistletoe>=1.6"]

The provable property, asserted over a hostile corpus: after parsing the rendered
Markdown, **every untrusted sentinel appears only inside `CodeFence` token content**, and
the set of non-fence structural tokens is exactly the trusted chrome — identical
regardless of what the input contained. Concretely: no `Heading` whose content is not a
known chrome literal; no `List`, `Quote`, `Table`, `Link`, `Image`, `HtmlSpan`, or
`HtmlBlock` anywhere derived from input; the heading sequence is byte-identical across
benign and hostile inputs.

Hostile corpus must include, in EVERY untrusted field: headings, list markers, blockquote
markers, table pipes, links, images, autolinks, raw HTML, code fences of several lengths,
indentation variants of 1-3 spaces before a marker, bare CR, CRLF, LF, backslash runs
adjacent to metacharacters, and nested combinations.

Every new regression test must fail against the pre-fix tree and pass after.

## E. What must not change

- The `recallweave.contract.v1` JSON schema and its semantics. The JSON document is
  authoritative and does not change to accommodate rendering.
- Every non-rendering behavior: builder, exclusions, budget, provenance, destination
  protocol, evidence classes, and all existing command output.
- Runtime dependency-free installation. `pip install recallweave` must still pull nothing.
acceptance_criteria: No untrusted value renders outside a fenced code block, proven by AST assertions over a hostile corpus; heading sequence identical for benign and hostile input; runtime install pulls no third-party packages; CI installs the test extra and the parser-backed tests do not skip; JSON schema and all non-rendering behavior unchanged; Codex returns PASS.

For a project whose premise is evidence-class separation, a projection that cannot distinguish what the operator asserted from the evidence attached to it is a defect of the first order.

title: Remediate adversarial review FAIL on task contracts
description: Codex returned FAIL on the integrated task contract capability. Two release-blocking issues (Markdown structure injection outside passage fences; unsanitized and unbudgeted connection evidence), two high issues (false authorization language; safe_write behavior regression), five medium issues, and a set of missing adversarial tests. Every finding was independently reproduced before this epic was opened. Three of the defects trace to errors in the v1 frozen interface rather than to the implementation.
design:
# FROZEN INTERFACE v2 — task contract remediation (supersedes v2 sections below)

This amends the v1 frozen interface in epic recallweave-olk after an adversarial review
returned FAIL. Only the rules below change; everything else in the v1 design field stands.
Three of these defects trace to v1 being WRONG, not to the workers. Implement v2 literally.

Test command: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
Baseline on current main: 209 tests OK. Every bead must leave the suite green.

## A. Markdown safety model — REPLACES v1 section 8's rendering rule

v1 said "sanitize in the builder, fence the passages". That was wrong. Sanitizing strips
control characters but deliberately preserves newlines, and newlines are Markdown
structure. Confirmed reproduction: a spec objective containing "\n## 9. Forged section"
renders as a real level-2 heading, producing 9 top-level sections instead of the frozen 8.
The same forging works through acceptance criteria, constraint and prior-decision
statements (which can be vault text), citations, and connection endpoints.

New rule: the renderer treats EVERY string it receives as untrusted and escapes it for the
position it occupies. Sanitizing upstream does not make a string safe to interpolate.

  - Multi-line block fields (objective, and any statement containing a newline):
    render inside a fence, using the existing longest-backtick-run rule.
  - Single-line inline fields (acceptance criteria, single-line statements, headings
    derived from citations): collapse all newlines to a single space, then escape the
    Markdown block-structure characters that could start a construct at line start
    (#, >, -, *, +, digits followed by '.' or ')', |, and backticks).
  - Table cells (connection source/target/kind/verified): collapse newlines AND escape
    the pipe character; a cell must never be able to add or split a column.
  - Citations rendered inline in backticks: collapse newlines and neutralize backticks so
    the code span cannot be closed early.

Invariant the tests must assert: for ANY document content whatsoever, the rendered
Markdown contains exactly 8 lines beginning with "## " and exactly one line beginning
with "# ", and every "### " line comes from the retrieved-context section.

## B. Connection evidence — REPLACES v1 assembly rule 4

v1 said connections use "the same shape query.py already uses". That shape is
`json.loads(row["evidence_json"])` — a raw passthrough of index-authored evidence. It
carries two ~501-character raw vault passages per candidate edge plus heading text, none
of it sanitized and none of it counted. Confirmed: U+202E, U+200B and U+0007 survive in
connections[].evidence.source_evidence.passage while being correctly stripped from
retrieved_context[].passage; and 1495 characters of evidence were emitted against a stated
600-character budget.

New rule: build a bounded, whitelisted, sanitized contract-specific evidence shape.
viewer._edge_evidence already solves exactly this problem — follow its approach, do not
invent a new one:

  - whitelist keys: citation, heading, passage, truncated on each of source_evidence and
    target_evidence; plus shared_terms (bounded to 12), method, explanation at the top.
  - run every string through contract_text.sanitize.
  - bound each passage with contract_text.bounded at MAX_PASSAGE_CHARACTERS.
  - count every emitted evidence string against the budget (see C).
  - drop anything not on the whitelist rather than passing it through.

## C. Budget definition — REPLACES v1 assembly rule 5's counting sentence

v1 defined characters_used as passages + statements + objective + directives. That excludes
edge evidence, which is the single largest vault-derived payload in the document. A budget
that does not bound the thing it is handed to another agent is not a budget.

New definition: characters_used is the total length of every VAULT-DERIVED or
OPERATOR-AUTHORED text string emitted in the document — retrieved passages, constraint and
prior-decision statements, cited passages, connection evidence passages and headings, the
objective, acceptance criteria statements, and exclusion directives. Structural metadata
(paths, citations, matched terms, kinds, scores, schema strings) is NOT counted; say so
explicitly where it is computed and in the documentation.

Connections are emitted only while budget remains; when the budget is exhausted, stop
adding connections and set budget.truncated true. Document that connections are the last
thing to be admitted, so a small budget yields context without evidence rather than a
document that silently exceeds its stated bound.

Also: includes_operator_statements must account for the always-present objective, or the
flag must be renamed to what it actually reports. Pick one and make schema, code, receipt
and docs agree.

## D. Authorization language — the v1 handling.scope string was FALSE

v1 specified: "This bundle is the complete authorized context for this task. Do not access,
request, or infer vault content outside it." That asserts an authorization decision the
tool cannot make, and it contradicts SECURITY.md:73, ARCHITECTURE.md:32 and line 319 of
docs/task-contracts.md itself. RecallWeave does not authorize anything; a private broker
does. This sentence was an architect error, not an implementation error.

Replacement handling.scope, verbatim:
    "This bundle contains the context the operator selected for this task. It is a scoped
     projection of an index, not an authorization decision, and it does not certify that
     anything outside it is forbidden or that everything inside it is permitted."

Every doc sentence describing a bundle as complete, authorized, or a boundary must change
with it.

## E. safe_write parity — REPLACES v1 section 6's `label` note

The extraction changed a user-visible message and added a path disclosure:
    before: "Viewer output cannot replace the RecallWeave database."
    after:  "Viewer output cannot replace the protected file: /absolute/path"
My v1 acceptance criterion ("test_viewer.py passes with an empty diff") did not catch this
because no existing test asserted that string. Diff-of-tests is not behavior parity.

New rules:
  - Every exception message reachable through export_viewer_graph must be byte-identical
    to 00d8fe7. Where a message needs to differ per caller, pass the full message text or a
    message template in, not a noun to interpolate into a new sentence.
  - No exception message may include an absolute path that the pre-extraction code did not
    already include.
  - safe_write must not import viewer. The current `_current_installer()` doing
    `from . import viewer` reverses the extraction boundary and exists only to satisfy
    monkeypatching. Make the installer an injectable parameter or a module-local
    indirection inside safe_write, and update the tests to patch that instead.

## F. Remaining corrections

  - statement truncation must be reported: if an operator statement or a cited statement is
    shortened, the item's truncated flag must say so. Today it is always false for operator
    text and reflects only passage truncation for cited items.
  - spec.notes is validated, documented, and present in the example, but never emitted.
    Either emit it in the document (as operator-authored text, counted against the budget)
    or reject it in the spec. Do not leave a field that silently does nothing.
  - retrieval fetches limit * 2 ranked hits before exclusion filtering, so heavy exclusion
    can return fewer than `limit` results while valid lower-ranked hits exist. Fetch until
    the post-exclusion limit is satisfied or the ranked results are exhausted, with a hard
    upper bound so the query stays bounded.
  - suppressed_total sums retrieved_context + connections + notes, but `notes` counts unique
    notes already counted in retrieved_context. Either report the categories without a
    misleading total, or define the total as a non-overlapping count.
acceptance_criteria: Both criticals fixed and covered by adversarial tests that fail against the current tree; authorization language removed from output and docs; viewer exception messages byte-identical to 00d8fe7 with no added path disclosure; safe_write no longer imports viewer; budget covers all vault-derived emitted text; all five medium findings resolved; full suite green; Codex re-review passes.

title: Connection cap precedes exclusions; text items silently discard note-only fields
description:
Two findings from the independent PR reviewer on #1, deliberately NOT fixed in
that PR. Both are real and reproduced by inspection; neither is an
exclusion-integrity or evidence-integrity breach, and both need a behavioural
decision rather than a mechanical fix.

1. contract.py -- APPLY THE CONNECTION CAP AFTER EXCLUSIONS.
   _edge_rows applies its 200-row limit BEFORE the loop performs exclusion
   filtering. When a retrieved note has at least 200 higher-ranked edges whose
   endpoints are all excluded, plus a lower-ranked allowed edge, every fetched
   row is suppressed and the allowed connection is omitted despite ample
   character budget. The artifact is missing a connection it should carry.

   Not a leak -- the failure is UNDER-inclusion -- which is why it is filed
   rather than fixed alongside the integrity findings.

2. contract_spec.py -- REJECT NOTE-ONLY FIELDS ON TEXT ITEMS.
   `{"text": "keep", "statement": "important qualification"}` passes validation
   because the discriminator checks only text-vs-note. _resolve_item then takes
   the text branch and silently DISCARDS both `statement` and `heading`. The
   documented item shapes make those fields applicable only to note selectors,
   so an operator-authored qualification is accepted and thrown away.
design:
Each needs a decision before implementation.

1. Connection cap. Options: fetch through excluded rows (over-fetch, then cap
   the POST-exclusion projection); or push exclusion into the _edge_rows query
   so the cap applies to allowed rows only. The second is cleaner and keeps the
   bound meaningful, but exclusion currently evaluates tags in Python via
   _note_excluded, so pushing it down means expressing path/glob/tag exclusion
   in SQL or pre-computing an excluded note-id set. Pre-computing the excluded
   set and adding `AND source_note_id NOT IN (...) AND target_note_id NOT IN
   (...)` is probably the smallest correct change. Note MAX_EDGE_ROWS is a
   documented bound -- whatever is chosen, the docs must still describe the cap
   truthfully.

2. Note-only fields on text items. Rejecting is the honest behaviour, and
   matches how `spec.notes` is REJECTED rather than ignored (handoff decision
   7). But it is a COMPATIBILITY change: a spec that is accepted today would
   start failing. Decide whether that is acceptable pre-1.0 -- it almost
   certainly is, since the fields are silently discarded today, so nobody can
   be relying on them working.

Reproduce both before implementing, per the standing rule.
acceptance_criteria: A test builds a note with 200+ higher-ranked excluded edges plus one allowed lower-ranked edge and asserts the allowed connection is exported. A test asserts a text item carrying 'statement' or 'heading' is rejected rather than silently discarding them. Both FAIL against the current tree. Docs describe the cap truthfully. Full suite green.
notes:
Josh 2026-08-23: remain deferred until post-stewardship triage; connection-cap ordering and note-only field rejection are real but not blocking checkpoint durability.
Josh 2026-08-23: pulled forward from deferred; decisions affirmed — cap after exclusions via excluded-note-id precompute; reject note-only fields on text items (pre-1.0 compatibility OK).

title: Platform-dependent assumptions the local gate cannot observe
description:
Raised by the post-merge re-gate (cycle 31) as follow-up, NOT as a blocker. No
current failure; these are coverage gaps the local gate structurally cannot see.

The lesson that produced them: a green local suite is not evidence about
platforms the local suite does not run. Three hostile-filename tests errored on
Windows for the whole of cycles 14-30 while passing on macOS and Linux, because
the fixture carried a ':' that Windows forbids in filenames. The local gate ran
macOS only, and the Codex gate reads the local gate's results, so neither could
see it. It surfaced only when a milestone PR met the required checks.

Remaining platform-dependent assumptions the reviewer named:

1. Case-insensitive filesystems. A vault containing paths that differ only by
   case behaves differently on macOS (usually case-insensitive) and Linux
   (case-sensitive). Note resolution and exclusion matching both key off
   relative paths.
2. Windows junctions. The destination protocol explicitly promises junction
   refusal, but the existing test skips when ordinary symlink creation is
   unavailable, so it may never exercise a real junction on Windows.
3. A line-ending matrix. Build equivalent indexed evidence from LF and CRLF
   source files and compare the documented deterministic output byte for byte.
   CRLF/CR normalization is load-bearing for fence safety and injectivity.
4. The `viewer` CI job runs only on ubuntu-latest, yet contains a WINDOWS
   static-asset regression test ("production server delivers every rendered
   client asset"). The thing it guards is not exercised on the platform it is
   about.
design:
Treat this as test-coverage work, not product work. Nothing here is known to be
broken; the point is that the local gate cannot observe these, so they must be
observed in CI or by construction.

Preferred order, cheapest and most likely to find something first:

1. Line-ending matrix -- pure Python, no platform dependency, and it exercises
   normalization that is already load-bearing.
2. A portability guard for OTHER fixtures, generalizing
   HostileFilenamePortabilityTest: any test that writes a vault file with a
   computed name should have that name checked against the Windows reserved
   set, the C0 controls, and trailing space/dot. That converts a
   platform-specific failure into a local one, which is the whole value of the
   existing guard.
3. Case-insensitive filesystem behaviour, pinned as a decision first: decide
   what SHOULD happen for two notes differing only by case, then test it.
4. Windows junction coverage, which needs the test to create a real junction on
   Windows rather than skipping.
5. Extend the `viewer` job to windows-latest, or move its Windows static-asset
   test somewhere that runs on Windows.

Do NOT bundle this into a milestone PR. It ages whatever review verdict is
current, which is exactly what happened to the cycle-30 PASS.
acceptance_criteria: A line-ending matrix compares LF and CRLF derived output byte for byte. Fixture filename portability is guarded generally, not only for the one hostile-filename constant. Case-insensitive path behaviour is decided and pinned. Windows junction refusal is exercised on Windows rather than skipped. The viewer's Windows static-asset test runs on Windows, or the job is extended there. Full suite green on all three platforms.
close_reason: Closed

title: A connection evidence side may omit a leaf and pass attribution
description:
Cycle-19 Medium, reproduced. The level below the cycle-18 fix.

recallweave-e5w made every SUPPLIED evidence leaf be compared against the
index. A leaf that is simply OMITTED was still never checked, because both the
well-formedness rules and the attribution comparison only looked at leaves the
side happened to carry.

Reproduced: take an authentic long indexed passage, keep its exact bounded text
(ellipsis included) and its citation, and delete only "truncated". The export
succeeds and emits a side with keys ['citation','heading','passage'] -- a
shortened passage with nothing declaring it shortened, contradicting
ARCHITECTURE.md's promise that a shortened passage sets truncated to true. It is
a false claim by silence. Deleting only "heading" likewise produces a side shape
the indexer never emits.

Compounding this, the complete-shape rule was NOT enforced by any test: removing
it from the predicate left all 397 tests green, because the builder's
leaf-by-leaf comparison happened to catch the same shapes through a different
path. That is the self-fulfilling pattern this project keeps rediscovering -- an
invariant asserted at one level while the defect lives at another.
design:
Require a present connection-evidence side to reproduce the COMPLETE shape
index.py's cited_passage() emits -- exactly citation, heading, passage and
truncated -- rather than a permitted subset, and compare all four
unconditionally in the attribution check.

index.py's cited_passage() always emits all four when it resolves a section at
all (it returns {} otherwise, and _edge_evidence then omits the side entirely),
so this rejects no real evidence.

Add a PREDICATE-LEVEL test that drives each leaf out in turn, on both sides, so
the rule is enforced where it lives rather than incidentally through the
builder. Prove it by mutation: removing the rule, or relaxing it from an exact
set to a subset check, must fail that test.

Update docs/task-contracts.md, which documented all four leaves as optional, and
the CHANGELOG.
acceptance_criteria: A test drops each of citation, heading, passage and truncated in turn, on both evidence sides, for both a truncated and a non-truncated passage, and requires the export to fail closed; it FAILS against the current tree. A predicate-level test pins the same rule and FAILS when the rule is removed or relaxed to a subset check. A positive test asserts every side the public builder emits carries exactly the four leaves. Docs and CHANGELOG match. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. A present connection-evidence side must carry exactly citation, heading, passage and truncated; all four compared unconditionally. Predicate-level test added and mutation-proven (rule removal and subset relaxation both fail it) -- the rule was previously unenforced by any test. Docs and CHANGELOG updated. Suite 398 green.

title: Partition and invariance proofs are weaker than the docs claim
description:
Cycle-15 Medium, reproduced. Two independent weaknesses in the proofs added by
recallweave-3xl.

(a) The partition is proved over ONE populated builder corpus. _canonical_leaves
treats an empty collection as the leaf `X[]`, so a minimal but publicly
constructible document -- no query matches, no criteria, no constraints, no
decisions, no connections, no citations -- carries leaves that are in NEITHER
inventory. Reproduced against a single-note vault with a non-matching query:

  unclassified: acceptance_criteria[], connections[], constraints[],
                prior_decisions[], retrieved_context[]

so the "exhaustive partition" claim in docs/task-contracts.md is false for that
shape.

(b) Every list probe in _not_projected_pair uses two ONE-ELEMENT non-empty
lists, and the scalar probes never use an empty or falsy value. A renderer that
read only len(value), bool(value) or emptiness would render both probes
identically and the invariance test would pass while the omitted field
influenced the Markdown. Reproduced: adding

  if item.get("matched_terms"): parts.append(_literal("(had matched terms)"))

to _render_retrieved leaks a documented-omitted field into the artifact, and
test_documented_not_projected_fields_cannot_influence_output still passes.

Both are proof-integrity defects, not demonstrated renderer leaks: static
inspection says today's renderer reads neither.
design:
(a) Decide and enforce: a collection CONTAINER is not itself a leaf; its item
fields are. Build the canonical leaf set as the UNION over several public
builder shapes (populated, minimal/no matches, no connections, no criteria,
empty exclusions), then drop any `X[]` entry for which some longer leaf
`X[].…` exists in the union. What remains as a bare `X[]` is a SCALAR
collection whose own name is the field (exclusions.paths[], provenance.
citations[], retrieved_context[].matched_terms[], connections[].evidence.
shared_terms[]) and must still be classified. This makes the partition hold
across shapes instead of over one lucky corpus, and it cannot mask an
unclassified scalar list, because a scalar list has no `X[].` children.

(b) Replace the two-value probe with a MULTI-VALUE, MULTI-CARDINALITY one:
every omitted field is driven to at least three distinct values and all
renderings must be byte-identical. Lists get [], one element, and two elements.
Integers include 0. Strings include "". That kills a renderer reading
truthiness, length or emptiness, which the pair could not.

Update the docs so the "proved unreadable" claim describes what is actually
proved.
acceptance_criteria: The partition test runs over several public builder shapes including a minimal one with empty collections, and FAILS against the current tree for that shape. The invariance proof drives every omitted field to at least three distinct values including empty/falsy ones, and a renderer that leaks only the truthiness of an omitted list FAILS it (mutation-proven). Docs describe what is actually proved. Full suite green.
close_reason: Fixed on foundry/task-contracts. Partition now runs over five public builder shapes with an explicit container-vs-scalar-collection rule and proves the empty-collection case is exercised; invariance probes vary cardinality and falsiness. Six mutations killed, four of which the previous pair probe let through. Suite 382 green.

title: Documented projected/omitted field sets are not an exhaustive partition
description:
Cycle-14 Medium, reproduced. docs/task-contracts.md says "The omitted fields
are:" and then lists only ten retrieved_context leaves. The builder emits
several other canonical fields that the Markdown does not project and the docs
do not list, including at minimum:

- connections[].evidence.source_evidence.truncated
- connections[].evidence.target_evidence.truncated
- connections[].evidence.method
- connections[].evidence.explanation

canonical contract leaves, enforced by a test rather than maintained by hand.

   walking to leaves with a `[]` convention identical to PROJECTED_FIELDS.

title: Disclosure test must prove omission, not match today's formatting
description:
Cycle-13 Codex Medium. The repaired disclosure test still verifies TODAY'S REPRESENTATION rather than the property it claims.

It detects most omissions by searching for the current textual serialization, and retrieved_context[].truncated is detected only via a narrow label pattern ending in 'truncated' (test_contract_projection.py:1013). Either of these would disclose a documented-omitted field while EVADING the test:
  - a renderer that emits 'Passage 1 was truncated:'
  - a formatted integer such as 1,234,567 for line_start

The claimed property is that the renderer never reads or emits those fields. The test only asserts that one particular rendering of them is absent, so it is defeated by any presentation change -- which is precisely how the previous sentinel version failed (cycle-12: injected 1111, searched NPS_LINESTART).

This is the presentation-coupling version of the recurring pattern: the assertion is one level above the property.
design: Assert the property, not the formatting. Prefer an approach that cannot be evaded by re-serialization -- for example prove the omitted field's VALUE cannot influence the output at all: render twice with the omitted field set to two distinct values and assert the rendered bytes are identical. That holds regardless of how a renderer might choose to format the field, and it fails the moment the renderer starts reading it. Apply it uniformly to all ten documented-omitted fields, so none depends on a hand-written needle. Keep a presentation-level check only as a secondary signal, never as the primary guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: For every documented-omitted field, changing its value between two otherwise identical documents leaves the rendered Markdown byte-identical, and deliberately making the renderer emit that field breaks the test -- demonstrate by mutation for at least line_start, truncated and one string field. No omitted field's detection depends on a specific label or serialization. The test must FAIL against a renderer patched to emit 'Passage 1 was truncated:' and against one emitting a thousands-separated integer. Full suite green with the parser.

title: Projection tests must actually detect what they claim to detect
description:
Two cycle-12 Codex Mediums, both reproduced. Both are cases where a test's stated guarantee is not the guarantee it provides.

1. SENTINEL TYPE MISMATCH (test_contract_projection.py:765 vs :816). The disclosure test searches for string sentinels but the population helper injects values of a different type, so the search can never match:
     line_start: injects 1111, searches 'NPS_LINESTART'
     line_end:   injects 2222, searches 'NPS_LINEEND'
     truncated:  injects True, searches 'NPS_TRUNCATED'
   Verified in the tree: lines 779-781 define those sentinels, lines 823-824 inject 1111/2222. A renderer change that started emitting line_start, line_end or truncated would NOT fail this test. 4 of the 10 documented-omitted fields are effectively unchecked. Booleans and integers cannot carry arbitrary string sentinels; a renderer may legitimately serialize them as true/false.

2. LOST DRIFT CHECK (regression). docs/task-contracts.md:293 and test_contract_projection.py:121 both state the documented projected list and PROJECTED_FIELDS are compared so they cannot drift. That comparison NO LONGER EXISTS: _documented_projected_fields() was removed and the replacement parses only the not-projected section. Confirmed absent -- grep for _documented_projected_fields returns nothing. The two projected lists can now drift silently, which is precisely the self-referential weakness recallweave-ah5 was created to eliminate.
design: For (1), stop relying on a string needle for non-string fields. Either compare parsed rendered field labels, or use type-correct expected serializations per field, so an integer or boolean field is detected by what the renderer would actually emit. Whatever the mechanism, a deliberate addition of each omitted field to the renderer must fail the test -- prove that by mutation, one field at a time. For (2), restore a direct equality assertion between the documented projected-field list and PROJECTED_FIELDS, parsed from the docs the same way the not-projected list is, so neither can drift.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the ten documented-omitted fields is detectable: for each, temporarily rendering it makes the disclosure test fail (demonstrate by mutation, including line_start, line_end and truncated). A direct equality test between the documented projected list and PROJECTED_FIELDS exists and fails when either drifts -- show it failing against an injected drift before the fix. No string sentinel is used for a non-string field. Full suite green with the parser.
close_reason: Closed
